text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Four children died in two road accidents on Thursday.
- A quarter of Finns' pets are overweight and the portion is growing. Almost half of cats are too fat, veterinary says.
- Some indebted and alienated jobless would be starving without aid from parishes and organisations.
- Nordic natural gas pipeline network could be extended to the Baltic countries, Finnish and Danish Prime Ministers Paavo Lipponen and Poul Nyrup Rasmussen say. @
- No progress in talks between banks and unions on banks' charges for service, which unions say break an old agreement made when employers started paying wages to bank accounts.
- Helsinki hospital emergency service reform has brought chaos to Helsinki University hospital's emergency ward, number of patients has almost doubled since turn of the year.
- Telecommunications group Nokia breaks European Union directives in its selection of Finnish retailers, says researcher at the Office for Free Competition. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Merita's brokerage says expects the best investment returns in small caps: would be boosted by recovering home markets and improved profitability, with a growth peak in 1998.
- Now-bankrupt barbecue-bag maker Hope Finlandia was already in dire straits in 1995 when President Martti Ahtisaari gave it the Innosuomi award for entrepreneurship and innovativeness.
- Swiss Bank Hoffmann among 10 largest owners of food group HK Ruokatalo after its main owner LSO sold large stake in the firm on its first day on the brokers' list. @
AAMULEHTI
- Tampere Taxi centre is recording phone calls and has given some material to the police; authorities have doubts.
- Opposition Centre Party due to decide its position on European economic and monetary union (EMU) at an extraordinary party congress this autumn.
- Total immigration to Finland halved last year but the population still grew by 15,000. @
TURUN SANOMAT

- Green Party accepts more coal power as an interim solution for Finland's growing energy needs, but new plants should be built so they can easily be converted to natural gas, says the party's only minister, Minister of Environment Pekka Haavisto.
DEMARI
- Finland and Estonia agreed to lift visa requirements from the beginning of May. @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Parliament to debate EMU this spring but parties have not reached agreement on the debate's legislative status.
- Massive demand absorbs all this year's money for state credits for women entrepreneurs -- all spent in under two months.
-- Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 242
